points.text: Central claims (transformers learn like brains, genes unnecessary) overreach the evidence
Matching qualitative properties does not show same mechanism or neural-level structure
No comparison to newborn neural or behavioural data
Results likely hold for any hierarchical learner; do not discriminate hypotheses
No comparison to CNNs or other architectures trained on same data
No comparison to other objectives or generic learners such as ICA/sparse coding
No training controls on natural videos, noise or static images
Scrambled control confounded; smooth non-wave motion and spatially-destroyed controls missing
Untrained ViT is a weak baseline for 'no structure'
Edge metric uses arbitrary hand-chosen RDM without sensitivity analysis or statistics
Edge stimuli 0-90 degree range without wraparound and rotation artefacts problematic
No unit-level tuning, filter/Gabor fits, or V1 comparison
Shape test weak: 16 synthetic objects, mean-pooled patch-token RDMs
Shape bias may stem from colour insensitivity of greyscale training; colour input handling unclear
Shape bias is not IT-like shape selectivity; no generalisation tests
Gradient spread in globally-connected transformer is not a receptive field
Normalisation of signed gradients for RF size questionable
RF measure uses single stimulus and depends on object and position
Retinotopy claimed but never tested
RF measure not validated on known model; no error bars; units unclear
No variability, confidence intervals or statistical tests across seeds
'Early' and 'later' layers never defined
Ordered non-iid training stream, constant LR, 100 epochs without ablation
Single simulator preset; wave statistics, time window, rasterisation unjustified or undescribed
Selectional vs instructional framing false dichotomy; inductive biases analogous to genetic instruction
'No hardcoded priors' ignores patch tokenisation and position embeddings
Limited novelty over prior retinal-wave training and emergent locality work
Prior CNN/ICA retinal-wave models dismissed without empirical comparison
Related work thin and heavily self-citing
Methods underspecified: loss form, negatives, channels, rendering, layers, t-SNE settings
Broader-impact prenatal-phase claim untested; no downstream transfer experiment
Paper dominated by framing and discussion
Backprop training limits biological plausibility
Unsupervised temporal learning method not described in methods
'Self-organization' conflated with representational similarity; no topographic organization analysis
No comparison of model RSMs to human brain data
Missing control training on other stimuli like gratings or natural videos
Figure 4(d) bar plots too low-resolution
Incremental over Ligeralde et al.: CNN swapped for ViT
No comparison against prior models trained on retinal waves
100 training epochs biologically implausible; developmental trajectory ignored
Very low-resolution inputs; unclear if findings scale
Receptive-field analysis limited to fovea; eccentricity not considered
Excluding CLS token from RF analysis undermines validity
Mischaracterises Ligeralde et al. as not using spatiotemporal waves
Temporally shuffled control cannot isolate spatial statistics; reconstruction objective needed
